h: Ancient sites all around the Preseli foothills
p: Castell Henllys works brilliantly as the start of a day exploring the prehistoric side of north Pembrokeshire. This corner of Wales is crammed with ancient sites, and once the kids have had a taste of Iron Age life in the roundhouses, they'll be primed for more. The village is run by the Pembrokeshire Coast National Park Authority, and it's well known for the school groups that come to try out Iron Age life, so there's a real hands-on feel to the place.

A short drive away, Pentre Ifan is one of the most impressive Neolithic burial chambers in Wales, with a huge capstone balanced on upright stones and views towards the Preseli Hills. It's even older than the Iron Age village and gives a fascinating sense of just how long people have lived here. The Preseli Hills themselves are famously linked to Stonehenge, as some of its bluestones are believed to have come from these slopes.

Nearby Nevern is a lovely village with a church known for its ancient yew trees, including the so-called bleeding yew that oozes red sap, and a beautifully carved Celtic cross in the churchyard. It's a peaceful spot for a short stop.

Newport is a small, friendly town with places to eat and a sandy beach at Newport Sands, and the Pembrokeshire Coast Path runs right past, offering cliff walks with seabirds and seals. Cardigan, a bustling market town with a restored castle, is a short drive in the other direction, perfect for a bit of shopping and a cuppa.
